# Adjudication Task — Chapter 770

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃770화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“스켈레톤 킹은, 그는 몬스터니까요.”
  6|
  7|힘없이 사그라지는 그 목소리를 끝으로 찾아온 고요.
  8|
  9|그러나 최민우의 마지막 한마디는, 누군가의 귓가에 마치 메아리치듯 계속해서 울려 퍼지고 있었다.
 10|
 11|‘몬스터…… 몬스터라.’
 12|
 13|마음속으로 뇌까린 스켈레톤 킹은 씁쓸한 진실을 곱씹었다.
 14|
 15|맞다. 그는 몬스터다.
 16|
 17|인류 역사상 최대(最大)이자 최악(最惡)의 적.
 18|
 19|그것이 바로 몬스터고, 자신은 그중에서도 저주받은 죽음의 힘을 다루는 존재였다.
 20|
 21|비록 지금은 인간의 모습을 하고 있을지라도, 전신을 감싼 이 마법이 걷히면 드러나는 것은 필멸(必滅)의 운명을 거스른 망자의 해골뿐.
 22|
 23|오직 그것만이 유일한 진실이었다.
 24|
 25|‘그래, 이것뿐이겠지.’
 26|
 27|인간이나 다름없는 자신의 두 손을 말없이 내려다보던 스켈레톤 킹은 불현듯 고개를 들었다.
 28|
 29|익숙한 얼굴, 그러나 동시에 낯설게 느껴질 만큼 일그러진 표정을 한 젊은 인간이 보인다.
 30|
 31|자신이 본 존재 중 가장 강하고, 한편으로는 멍청하며, 그렇기에 눈앞의 진실을 받아들이지 못하는 인간.
 32|
 33|그러나 단 하나뿐인 돌파구로 나아가기 위해서는, 그 진실을 받아들이고 이용해야 했다.
 34|
 35|“저 인간의 말이 옳다. 모두 사실이야.”
 36|
 37|“……너.”
 38|
 39|억눌린 목소리에 담긴 수많은 감정들.
 40|
 41|몇 달 전만 하더라도 느끼지 못했던 그 감정의 이름을, 이제는 안다.
 42|
 43|말을 잇지 못하는 진태경을 향해 스켈레톤 킹은 고개를 저어 보였다.
 44|
 45|“네가 무슨 말을 하더라도, 이 방법뿐이다.”
 46|
 47|“……!”
 48|
 49|“이 몸은 몬스터다. 어떤 이유로도 우리가 함께하는 것은 용납될 수 없어.”
 50|
 51|물론 누군가는 진실이 밝혀져도 이해해 줄지도 모른다. 진태경을 믿고, 스켈레톤 킹이 자신들이 알던 몬스터와는 다른 존재라는 것을 받아들일 수도 있다.
 52|
 53|하지만…….
 54|
 55|“과연 그들 중 몇이나 이 진실을 받아들이겠느냐.”
 56|
 57|스켈레톤 킹은 닫혀 있는 창문을 가리켰다.
 58|
 59|저 밖에서 살아가는 대부분의 인간들은 지극히 평범하다. 그렇기에 몬스터를 뼛속 깊이 증오할 수밖에 없다.
 60|
 61|가족을, 친구를, 혹은 사랑하는 연인을 몬스터에 의해 잃었으니까.
 62|
 63|몬스터는 인간을, 인간 역시 몬스터를 죽인다.
 64|
 65|마왕 아스모데우스의 강림과 동시에 채워진 이 사슬은 그 누구도 풀 수 없을 만큼 두껍고 견고했다.
 66|
 67|설령 모두에게 사랑받는 젊은 영웅이라 해도 예외는 아니다.
 68|
 69|아니, 모든 것이 밝혀진다면 더 이상 예전과 같은 영웅으로 남을 수 없을 것이다.
 70|
 71|“많은 이들이 너희를 비난할 테고, 미카엘 실베르트가 모든 것을 얻겠지. 그러니…….”
 72|
 73|서서히 흐려지는 말꼬리. 진태경을 뒤로하고 돌아선 스켈레톤 킹은, 문고리에 손을 얹으며 마지막 한마디를 덧붙였다.
 74|
 75|“모두가 지켜보는 앞에서, 이 몸을 소멸시켜라.”
 76|
 77|탁.
 78|
 79|등 뒤에서 닫히는 문.
 80|
 81|말없이 복도를 가로지르는 내내 스켈레톤 킹은 돌아보지 않았다. 머리 위로 밝혀진 조명은 환했으나, 그의 앞에 놓인 길은 어두웠다.
 82|
 83|짙은 안개와 죽음의 기운으로 가득했던 그곳처럼.
 84|
 85|처음 눈을 뜬 그 순간부터 떠날 수 없게 되어 버린, 그러나 생각지도 못했던 어느 날 한 인간에 의해 떠나게 되었던 그 게이트처럼.
 86|
 87|‘나는 도대체 뭐지? 이름은? 과거는? 고향은?’
 88|
 89|그리고 언젠가부터 찾아온 그 의문에 대한 답을, 이제는 알 것 같았다.
 90|
 91|자신은 몬스터였다.
 92|
 93|이성이라고는 찾아볼 수 없는, 잔인하고 흉포한 몬스터.
 94|
 95|순수한 악(惡)으로부터 비롯된, 결코 인간과 함께할 수 없는 존재.
 96|
 97|그것이 진실이다. 아니, 진실이어야 한다.
 98|
 99|이제는 받아들일 수밖에 없는 현실을 마주한 스켈레톤 킹은 실소를 흘렸다.
100|
101|‘젠장. 이제 클럽은 영영 못 가겠군.’
102|
103|그런데 어째서일까. 가슴 한구석이 후련했다.
104|
105|자신은 심장은커녕, 평범한 감정조차 품지 못할 몬스터인데.
106|
107|분명 그래야 하는데.
108|
109|
110|
111|* * *
112|
113|
114|
115|굳이 어디선가 그 말을 듣지 않았더라도, 하루하루를 살아가다 보면 자연스럽게 알게 된다.
116|
117|인생은 매 순간 선택의 연속이라는 것을.
118|
119|선택이라고 다 거창한 것이 아니다. 사람에게는 아침에 눈을 뜨면서부터 자그마한 선택지가 주어진다.
120|
121|이대로 일어날까, 말까. 일어난다면 샤워를 할까. 아니면 세수와 머리만 감고 나갈까.
122|
123|그때그때 처한 상황에 따라 선택이 달라진다.
124|
125|예상보다 일찍 눈을 떴다면 조금 더 잘 수도 있고, 지각이 염려된다면 샤워를 건너뛰어도 상관없다.
126|
127|다만 선택하기 전에 앞서 생각해야 할 것은, 그 선택이 불러올 결과다.
128|
129|자신 스스로 감당할 수밖에 없는 결과.
130|
131|그리고 지금 이 순간. 나는 어느 것 하나 감당하기 힘든 선택의 기로에 서 있었다.
132|
133|“이…… 미친 새끼.”
134|
135|간신히 쥐어 짜낸 목소리가 입 밖으로 튀어나온다.
136|
137|그것은 이미 자리를 떠난 누군가를 향한 욕설이었고, 남아 있는 또 다른 누군가를 겨냥한 것일 수도 있었다.
138|
139|혹은, 이러지도 저러지도 못하는 나 자신을.
140|
141|“진태경 씨.”
142|
143|실타래처럼 얽힌 머릿속이 지끈거린다. 귓가를 파고드는 나직한 부름에 나는 말없이 눈을 감았다.
144|
145|“선택해야 합니다.”
146|
147|보이지 않는 송곳이 뇌리를 관통하는 듯했다.
148|
149|한 마디, 한 마디 이어지는 말에 두통이 더욱더 심해졌다.
150|
151|“그는 이미 길을 정했습니다. 오직 자신만이 결정할 수 있었던 희생을…….”
152|
153|와락, 쿵!
154|
155|나도 모르겠다.
156|
157|도대체 언제 눈을 뜬 건지, 그리고 어째서 내가 최 팀장의 멱살을 붙잡고 있는지.
158|
159|찌직.
160|
161|구겨진 명품 셔츠의 옷깃이 힘을 이기지 못해 찢겨 나간다. 하얗게 물든 손아귀의 위로, 묵묵히 나를 바라보는 한 쌍의 눈동자가 있었다.
162|
163|“내키는 대로 하십시오. 저를 곤죽이 되도록 두들겨 패도 좋고, 사지를 부러트리거나 설령 죽인다 해도 상관없습니다. 하지만…….”
164|
165|파르르 떨리는 숨결, 그리고 목소리가 이어졌다.
166|
167|“그 후에는 선택하셔야 합니다. 반드시.”
168|
169|“……!”
170|
171|“아시지 않습니까. 시간은 우리를 기다려 주지 않습니다.”
172|
173|그 말에, 그 눈빛에 맥이 탁 풀렸다.
174|
175|금방이라도 폭발할 것처럼 전신에 들끓던 기운도, 한껏 힘이 들어간 손아귀도 모든 것이 낯설게만 느껴졌다.
176|
177|나는 잠시 뭔가에 사로잡혀 있던 사람처럼 뒷걸음질 쳤다.
178|
179|힘없는 사과와 함께.
180|
181|“……미안합니다.”
182|
183|나도 안다. 최 팀장에게는 아무런 잘못도 없다는 것을.
184|
185|그가 말한 것은 모두 진실이었고, 이 상황을 돌파할 수 있는 유일한 해결책이었을 뿐이다.
186|
187|스켈레톤 킹이 스스로 희생하려는 뜻을 밝히지 않았다면 최 팀장 역시 아무 말도 하지 않았을 것이다.
188|
189|그는 그런 사람이니까.
190|
191|냉철한 판단력을 통해 유일한 해결책을 이미 알고 있었음에도, 다른 누군가에게 희생을 강요하지 않는 도덕성을 갖춘 사람이니까.
192|
193|누군가는 그런 그를 두고 위선자라 부를 수도 있겠지만, 적어도 나는 아니다.
194|
195|내가 그렇듯, 최 팀장에게 있어서도 스켈레톤 킹은 그저 죽여 없애야 하는 몬스터 따위가 아니라는 것을 아니까.
196|
197|‘설령 자신이 희생해야 하는 상황이라 해도, 누구보다 먼저 그것을 해결책으로 내놓았겠지.’
198|
199|나와 달리 그는 타고난 리더다.
200|
201|만약 내가 아닌 그에게 선택권이 있었다면, 그는 회피하지 않았을 것이다.
202|
203|홀로 괴로워할지언정 비겁하게 진실을 외면하지는 않았을 테다.
204|
205|‘빌어먹을.’
206|
207|시간은 우리를 기다려 주지 않는다.
208|
209|최 팀장의 그 말을 떠올리자 저 너머에서 나를 기다리고 있을 또 다른 세상이 눈앞을 스쳤다.
210|
211|무림(武林).
212|
213|만약 메인 퀘스트로 인해 로그인 기능이 막히지 않았더라면, 그곳에서 훨씬 긴 시간 동안 고민할 수 있다면 나는 어떤 선택을 할까.
214|
215|아니, 충분한 시간이 주어진다면 비로소 선택이라는 것을 할 수 있을까?
216|
217|‘그리고 그 결과를, 나는 감수할 수 있나.’
218|
219|지금껏 나는 수없이 많은 전투를 치렀다.
220|
221|살아남기 위해 발버둥 쳤고, 내 사람들을 지키기 위해 싸웠다.
222|
223|그러나 지금 내 앞에 놓인 두 갈래 길의 끝에는 고통만이 남아 있을 뿐이다.
224|
225|스켈레톤 킹을 희생시키지 않는다면 이 세상이 미카엘 실베르트의 손아귀에 넘어가고, 이대로 녀석을 희생시킨다면…… 나 스스로가 도무지 견딜 수 없을 것 같다.
226|
227|그래, 언제부터였는지는 몰라도 스켈레톤 킹은 내 친구였다.
228|
229|함께 싸운 전우이자 친구.
230|
231|단순히 대의(大意)라는 두 글자를 위해 희생시킬 수 없는 존재.
232|
233|‘그런 녀석을 소멸시켜야 한다. 그것도 모두가 보는 앞에서 직접.’
234|
235|인벤토리를 이용하여 소멸을 위장하는 같잖은 속임수 따위는 통하지 않는다. 미카엘 실베르트는 그 정도로 허술한 위인이 아니니까.
236|
237|내가 스켈레톤 킹을 완전히 통제한다는 것을 증명해도 상황은 달라지지 않을 것이다.
238|
239|인류에게 있어 몬스터는 건드려서는 안 될 역린(逆鱗)과도 같다.
240|
241|이미 수십여 년간의 실험을 통해 몬스터는 결코 길들일 수 없다는 사실 역시 증명되지 않았나.
242|
243|스켈레톤 킹은 전대미문(前代未聞)의 존재였고, 어떠한 종류의 진실은 알려짐과 동시에 배척받는다.
244|
245|‘결국…… 답은 하나뿐이야.’
246|
247|나는 눈을 감았다. 그리고 섬광처럼 뇌리를 스치는 수많은 고민 끝에, 불현듯 입을 열었다.
248|
249|“최 팀장님.”
250|
251|말없이 내 결정을 기다리던 그가 대답했다.
252|
253|“말씀하십시오.”
254|
255|“혹시 세계 헌터 연맹의 재설립 승인이 취소될 가능성이 있습니까?”
256|
257|“갑자기 그건 왜…….”
258|
259|“대답만.”
260|
261|단호한 말과 함께 감았던 눈을 떴다. 복잡한 시선으로 나를 응시하던 최 팀장이 입을 열었다.
262|
263|“승인이 취소될 가능성은 전무합니다.”
264|
265|“확실해요?”
266|
267|“네.”
268|
269|“이유는?”
270|
271|“이제 세계 헌터 연맹의 존재는 필수 불가결입니다. 나날이 마력 수치가 증가하는 현재의 상황과, 한 번 당겨진 불씨를 막을 수 있는 유일한 방법이니까요.”
272|
273|“만약, 이 상황에서 저나 그놈에게 무슨 일이 생긴다고 해도?”
274|
275|“……!”
276|
277|거세게 흔들리는 눈동자.
278|
279|얼마 지나지 않아 내 말의 의미를 깨달은 최 팀장이 버럭 소리쳤다.
280|
281|“진태경 씨!”
282|
283|하지만 나는 이미 선택했다. 첫 번째도, 두 번째도 아닌 세 번째 길을. 어두컴컴하고 가시밭길로 가득한 그 길을.
284|
285|그래.
286|
287|이 모든 것의 중심, 미카엘 실베르트를 죽인다.
288|
289|“안 됩니다!”
290|

[P89]

[P90]
Murim.

[P91]

[P92]

[P93]

[P94]
I’d fought countless battles. I’d struggled to survive and fought to protect my people.

[P95]
But both paths before me ended in pain.

[P96]
If I refused to sacrifice the Skeleton King, this world would fall into Michael Silbert’s hands. If I did sacrifice him… I didn’t think I could bear it.

[P97]
Somewhere along the way, the Skeleton King had become my friend.

[P98]
A comrade I’d fought beside. A friend.

[P99]
Not someone I could sacrifice for the sake of the greater good.

[P100]
*I’d have to erase him. Do it myself, in front of everyone.*

[P101]
A cheap trick like using the Inventory to fake his Erasure wouldn’t work. Michael Silbert wasn’t that careless.

[P102]
Proving I had complete control over the Skeleton King wouldn’t change anything, either.

[P103]
To humanity, monsters were a raw nerve no one could touch. Hadn’t decades of experiments already shown that monsters could never be tamed?

[P104]
The Skeleton King was unprecedented. But some truths were rejected the moment they became known.

[P105]

[P106]

[P108]

[P109]
“Yes?”

[P110]

[P111]
“Why do you suddenly—”

[P112]
“Just answer me.”

[P113]

[P114]
“There is no chance of that.”

[P115]
“You’re sure?”

[P116]
“Yes.”

[P117]
“Why?”

[P118]

[P119]

[P120]
“……!”

[P121]

[P122]
“Mr. Jin Taekyung!”

[P123]

[P124]

[P125]
I would kill Michael Silbert, the man at the center of it all.

[P126]
“No!”

[P127]

[P128]

[P129]

[P130]

[P131]

[P132]

[P133]

[P134]

[P135]

[P136]
“……!”

[P137]

[P140]

[P141]

[P142]

[P143]

[P144]

[P145]

[P148]

[P149]

Bzzzt.

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;

At the thought of his words, another world waiting for me beyond this one flashed before my eyes.

[P90]
Murim.

[P91]
If the main Quest hadn’t blocked the Login function, if I could spend far longer thinking about this there, what would I choose?

[P92]
No. Given enough time, would I even be able to choose?

[P93]
*And could I live with the result?*

[P94]
I’d fought countless battles. I’d struggled to survive and fought to protect my people.

[P95]
But both paths before me ended in pain.

[P96]
If I refused to sacrifice the Skeleton King, this world would fall into Michael Silbert’s hands. If I did sacrifice him… I didn’t think I could bear it.

[P97]
Somewhere along the way, the Skeleton King had become my friend.

[P98]
A comrade I’d fought beside. A friend.

[P99]
Not someone I could sacrifice for the sake of the greater good.

[P100]
*I’d have to erase him. Do it myself, in front of everyone.*

[P101]
A cheap trick like using the Inventory to fake his Erasure wouldn’t work. Michael Silbert wasn’t that careless.

[P102]
Proving I had complete control over the Skeleton King wouldn’t change anything, either.

[P103]
To humanity, monsters were a raw nerve no one could touch. Hadn’t decades of experiments already shown that monsters could never be tamed?

[P104]
The Skeleton King was unprecedented. But some truths were rejected the moment they became known.

[P105]
*In the end… there’s only one answer.*

[P106]
I closed my eyes. Countless thoughts flashed through my mind, and then I spoke.

[P107]
“Team Leader Choi.”

[P108]
He had been waiting in silence for my decision.

[P109]
“Yes?”

[P110]
“Is there any chance the approval to reestablish the World Hunter Federation could be revoked?”

[P111]
“Why do you suddenly—”

[P112]
“Just answer me.”

[P113]
I opened my eyes. Team Leader Choi studied me with a conflicted look before replying.

[P114]
“There is no chance of that.”

[P115]
“You’re sure?”

[P116]
“Yes.”

[P117]
“Why?”

[P118]
“The World Hunter Federation has become indispensable. With magical power levels rising every day, it’s the only way to contain the fire that has already been set.”

[P119]
“Even if something happens to me or that bastard?”

[P120]
“……!”

[P121]
His eyes widened. A moment later, he understood what I meant and shouted.

[P122]
“Mr. Jin Taekyung!”

[P123]
But I had already chosen.

[P124]
Neither the first path nor the second. A third one, dark and choked with thorns.

[P125]
I would kill Michael Silbert, the man at the center of it all.

[P126]
“No!”

[P127]
“Nothing’s impossible. It’s just difficult.”

[P128]
I answered calmly and kept going before he could interrupt.

[P129]
“If I pull this off… you’ll need to make your move, Team Leader Choi. Magic Johnson will do everything he can to help.”

[P130]
“Stop! Stop talking!”

[P131]
“There’s Chuck Hagel, Pai Chen, and Prince Felix too. Get the support of the S-rank Hunters you’ve built ties with and the nations friendly to us. Then take control of the reestablished World Hunter Federation.”

[P132]
“I don’t want to hear it! And how could I possibly…?”

[P133]
“Your maternal grandfather walked that path. If you can make people understand the weight of Cheon Taemin’s name, you have a shot. If that seems impossible, you could back Magic Johnson instead.”

[P134]
I grinned.

[P135]
“Well, you’re smart enough to figure it out yourself.”

[P136]
“……!”

[P137]
“Still, one more thing, just in case. Even if Michael Silbert loses his head, the rest of his organization will remain. You should find those people and get rid of them first—”

[P138]
Shing.

[P139]
A cold sound cut me off.

[P140]
A sword stood in my way.

[P141]
Team Leader Choi had drawn the *Hero’s Sword* without my noticing. He glared at me, his face set.

[P142]
“You’re not going.”

[P143]
“Hmm. I don’t think you can stop me.”

[P144]
“Nothing’s impossible. It’s just difficult.”

[P145]
He threw my words back at me. I stepped toward him.

[P146]
“Fine. I was going to rough you up anyway. This works out.”

[P147]
“What do you mean?”

[P148]
“Everyone knows we’re close. If I beat you half to a pulp before I leave, it might keep them from getting suspicious.”

[P149]
“……!”

[P150]
“……!”

[P151]
Team Leader Choi gritted his teeth. A dazzling aura flared around him, its immense power rippling along the blade and stirring the air.

[P152]
Rumble. Whoooosh!

[P153]
A tremor spread through the entire building. The wind rose into a gale.

[P154]
“You really do have talent. You’ve improved a lot.”

[P155]
I gave him a calm smile and was about to step forward when—

[P156]
Bzzzt.

[P157]
A faint vibration sounded from somewhere, cutting through the tension between us.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
